text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests, usually using methods like GET or POST. The server often responds with data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. However, before you can access most APIs, you need authentication, such as an API key or token, to prove your identity. You should also be aware of rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make in a certain time. Finally, always add error handling to your code, so your application can deal with failed requests gracefully.
